questions.stem: What is the bond energy of a covalent bond?

options.text: The energy released when the bond is formed
The energy required to break one mole of a particular covalent bond in gaseous molecules
The energy stored in the nucleus of an atom
The energy needed to melt a substance

questions.explanation: Bond energy is the amount of energy needed to break one mole of a particular type of covalent bond in gaseous molecules. It is measured in kJ/mol.

questions.stem: Is breaking bonds an endothermic or exothermic process?

options.text: Endothermic, because energy must be put in to break bonds
Neither, bonds break without any energy change
It depends on the type of bond

questions.explanation: Breaking bonds is always endothermic (requires energy input). Energy must be supplied to overcome the attraction between the bonded atoms. Conversely, making bonds is always exothermic (releases energy).

questions.stem: If more energy is released when making new bonds than is needed to break old bonds, the reaction is:
questions.explanation: If the energy released from making new bonds in the products is greater than the energy needed to break bonds in the reactants, there is an overall release of energy. This makes the reaction exothermic.

questions.stem: Why are bond energy values described as averages?

options.text: Because scientists cannot measure them accurately
Because the exact energy of a particular bond varies slightly depending on the molecule it is in
Because different scientists get different results

questions.explanation: Bond energies are averages because the exact energy of a bond (e.g. an O-H bond) varies slightly depending on the specific molecule and its chemical environment. The values given in data tables are averages taken from many different molecules.

questions.stem: Given: H-H bond energy = 436 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl = 242 kJ/mol, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol. For the reaction H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl, what is the energy needed to break all bonds in the reactants?
questions.explanation: Energy to break bonds: one H-H bond (436 kJ) + one Cl-Cl bond (242 kJ) = 678 kJ. You must break all the bonds in the reactant molecules before new bonds can form.

questions.stem: Using the same data (H-H = 436, Cl-Cl = 242, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol), what is the enthalpy change for H₂ + Cl₂ → 2HCl?
questions.explanation: Bonds broken: 436 + 242 = 678 kJ (endothermic). Bonds made: 2 x 431 = 862 kJ (exothermic). ΔH = energy in - energy out = 678 - 862 = -184 kJ. The negative value shows the reaction is exothermic.

questions.stem: A reaction has bonds broken = 500 kJ and bonds made = 400 kJ. What can you conclude?

options.text: The reaction is exothermic with ΔH = -100 kJ
The reaction is endothermic with ΔH = +100 kJ
The reaction is endothermic with ΔH = -100 kJ

questions.explanation: ΔH = energy to break bonds - energy released making bonds = 500 - 400 = +100 kJ. More energy is needed to break bonds than is released making new ones, so the overall reaction is endothermic (ΔH is positive).
